verses.text: The LORD told Joshua, “Don't be afraid or lose heart. Get up and take all the fighting men with you to Ai. I've handed over its king, its people, its city, and its land to you.
Treat Ai and its king as you treated Jericho and its king, except this time you can keep the goods and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city.”
Joshua and all the fighting men got ready to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand of his best fighters and sent them out at night.
He told them, “Wait in ambush behind the city. Stay close and be ready.
I'll approach the city with everyone who's with me. When they come out against us like they did the first time, we'll run from them.
They'll come after us until we've drawn them away from the city. They'll think, ‘They're running away from us just like last time.’ So we'll keep running.
Then come out of hiding and take the city. The LORD your God will hand it over to you.
Once you've taken the city, burn it. Do what the LORD has said. Those are your orders.”
Joshua sent them out, and they took up their position between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. Joshua spent that night with the people.
Joshua got up early, gathered the people, and went up to Ai with the elders of Israel at the head of the people.
All the fighting men with him marched up close to the city and camped to its north. A valley lay between them and Ai.
Joshua positioned about five thousand men in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
With the main army north of the city and the men in ambush to its west, Joshua went into the middle of the valley that night.

When the king of Ai saw what was happening, he and his people got up early and hurried out to fight Israel at the appointed time in front of the Arabah. He had no idea men were waiting behind his city.
Joshua and all Israel pretended they'd been beaten and ran toward the wilderness.
Everyone in the city was called out to chase them. As they went after Joshua, they were drawn away from the city.
Every man in Ai and Bethel went after Israel. They left the city wide open and kept chasing.
The LORD told Joshua, “Hold out the javelin in your hand toward Ai. I'll hand the city over to you.” Joshua held his javelin out toward the city.
As soon as he stretched out his hand, the men in ambush rushed out of hiding, ran into the city, and took it. They quickly set it on fire.
The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from the city into the sky. They had no way to escape in any direction. The Israelites who'd fled toward the wilderness turned on them.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that their men had taken the city and that smoke was rising, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
The other men came out of the city against them, leaving the men of Ai trapped between Israelites on both sides. Israel struck them down, leaving no survivors and letting no one escape.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
Israel finished killing the people of Ai who had chased them into the open country of the wilderness. When they'd all fallen by the sword, Israel went back to Ai and put the city to the sword.
Twelve thousand men and women fell that day, the entire population of Ai.
Joshua kept his javelin stretched out until all the people of Ai had been destroyed.
Israel kept only the livestock and goods from the city, just as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and turned it into a desolate heap of ruins that remains to this day.

He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset, Joshua ordered the body taken down and thrown at the entrance to the city gate. They piled stones over it, and that great heap is still there today.
Then Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel.

Moses, the LORD's servant, had commanded the Israelites to build it this way in his book of the law, using uncut stones untouched by an iron tool. They offered burnt offerings to the LORD on it and sacrificed peace offerings.
There, with the Israelites watching, Joshua wrote a copy of Moses' law on the stones.

All Israel stood on both sides of the ark in front of the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant. Their elders, officers, judges, native-born people, and foreigners were all there. Half stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses, the LORD's servant, had originally commanded when he told them to bless the people of Israel.
Then Joshua read every word of the law, including the blessing and the curse, just as it was written in the book of the law.
Joshua read every word Moses had commanded before the whole gathering of Israel, including the women, the children, and the foreigners living among them.
